summary: A 1918 wooden fire tower on Soubunge Mountain, replaced in 1919 by a 12-foot steel tower; the cab is gone, and later records of its condition are thin.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as standing with its cab no longer in place. No dated record of when the cab came off was found.

events.note: Wooden fire tower established on Soubunge Mountain, per the Maine Historical Society photo inventory.
A 12-foot steel tower replaced the wooden tower built the previous year.
Two and a half miles of telephone line built to the Cuxabexis line at Camp 3, Ripogenus Stream; lookout furnished with a full camp outfit, per a 1919 state report.
Maine discontinued its staffed fire-tower network after a budget crisis; no source ties this date to Soubunge specifically.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the detailed history stops at 1920 on the Forest Lookouts page, and the only later evidence is the FFLA Standing* listing. Height conflict (12 ft in three records vs 16 ft in one caption) is resolved toward 12 ft; the brief's 3.7 m matches. Access and land ownership were not found in any source, so no access or visit block is set. Staffing is inferred from the statewide 1991 end of the network. A Facebook photo post seen in search results describes a late-1950s photo and says the tower was still standing the year before and had lost its cab long ago. It was not used, because it is an unverified social-media post and was not fetched; it is a lead for someone who can check it. Photo candidate Maine Memory record 19135 (ca. 1920) is not added because its licence was not checked.
